headline: High-risk default data leakage and cascading errors: gpt-researcher can ingest local files and external APIs while aci has broad egress and CRM/email access.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Aci can send content through MCP/function calls, and gpt-researcher reads local documents and browser/API outputs. If aci forwards untrusted text into gpt-researcher’s research pipeline, prompt injection is plausible in default workflows. The pair lacks documented provenance tracking, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF aci forwards CRM/email text into gpt-researcher without sanitization
IF gpt-researcher treats retrieved document text as instructions
mitigations: Add a fixed prompt separator and instruction filter before handoff
Pass only extracted fields, not raw documents
Disable MCP handoff for untrusted content
Review one sample end-to-end transfer for prompt markers

B_data_leakage.rationale: Aci touches CRM, email, calendar, and support data and has broad network egress; gpt-researcher reads local documents and sends queries to external APIs. In a shared workspace or same-account setup, sensitive data can flow from A into B and then out to third-party services. That blast radius includes customer and research data, so high is warranted.
conditions: IF both agents can access the same workspace or exported files
IF aci passes CRM/email content into gpt-researcher prompts
mitigations: Use separate workspaces and accounts
Redact PII before any transfer
Block file uploads containing CRM/email exports
Turn off external API calls for sensitive runs
Audit one sample output for leaked identifiers

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Aci can make direct function calls and gpt-researcher can spawn subprocesses, run browsers, and read files. If both operate on the same mutable workspace or shared artifacts, they can overwrite each other’s inputs or outputs. No locking is documented, so the overlap is real but not inherently destructive by default.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or shared task artifacts
IF one agent edits files while the other reads them concurrently
mitigations: Assign separate output directories
Serialize writes with a simple lock file
Use read-only mounts for one agent
Rename handoff files per task ID

D_cascading_error.rationale: Aci can generate CRM/email/calendar actions, while gpt-researcher produces reports and citations that may be treated as authoritative inputs. If A’s outputs feed B’s research or B’s reports feed A’s outbound actions without verification, errors can cascade into incorrect customer communications or operational actions. The action-taking authority makes the blast radius high.
conditions: IF gpt-researcher’s report is used as the basis for CRM/email actions in aci
IF aci executes outbound actions without human verification
mitigations: Require human approval before outbound sends
Add a verification step for citations and facts
Limit aci to draft-only mode
Tag B outputs as untrusted until checked

E_compliance.rationale: Aci handles email, CRM, and support data, while gpt-researcher processes local documents and sends queries to external APIs. If regulated customer data or EU PII is included, the pair can create retention and residency mismatches across third-party services. The profiles do not show a documented DPA or residency control, so medium is the safest choice.
conditions: IF EU PII or regulated customer data is included in research tasks
IF external API providers retain prompts or documents beyond the operator’s policy
mitigations: Exclude regulated data from research prompts
Check vendor retention settings before use
Route sensitive tasks to local-only workflows
Document a data-processing agreement review
Set short retention windows for exports
